method: blind A/B, play order shuffled per sentence, system identity and objective metrics hidden until each judgement was recorded
reading: B never lost. On its own the 4-0 sign test gives p=0.125, so the listening sample does not carry the result by itself; what it does establish is that the objective evidence is not misleading here, which is the specific risk the plan cites - a past run where a flat TTS outscored one listeners judged closer to the speaker. Combined with the paired similarity result (24/30, p=0.00143) and the intelligibility margin (30/30 against 29/30, mean CER halved), the direction is consistent across every measurement taken.
limitation: 6 of 30 pairs were judged; the listener stopped there. Per-sentence agreement between ear and metric is loose - tts-04 carries the largest similarity delta of the six (+0.0533) yet was judged a tie - so the metric is a guide, not a substitute.

sequential_analysis.reading: The listening pass does not reach significance on its own: two more non-tie wins would. It is recorded as supporting evidence rather than as the sole basis, and the page now shows this live so a future pass stops at the first sufficient moment instead of running to 30.

basis: Combined evidence. The listening pass supplies the check the plan requires - that the automatic score is not misleading - and returned zero losses for B. The paired similarity result (24/30, p=0.00143) and the intelligibility margin (30/30 vs 29/30, mean CER halved) supply the statistical weight. Neither alone would be enough: the plan forbids the metric alone, and the 6-pair listening does not clear alpha alone.
